packs.title: Nuance in Conversation
packs.description: Common qualifiers for softening bad news, setting details aside, estimating, and drawing a tentative conclusion.

words.meaningMnemonic: A cook balances one tart on an eye and another on a knee, but both crash as you arrive. The cook groans <reading>EYE—KNEE—COOK</reading>: <vocabulary>unfortunately</vocabulary>, dessert is gone. あいにく often politely introduces inconvenient news or an unavailable option.

contextSentences.ja: あいにく、その日は予定があります。
contextSentences.en: Unfortunately, I already have plans that day.

contextSentences.ja: あいにく店長は外出しております。
contextSentences.en: I'm sorry, but the manager is out at the moment.

contextSentences.ja: 遠足の日はあいにくの雨だった。
contextSentences.en: Unfortunately, it rained on the day of the field trip.

words.meaningMnemonic: A frantic cook drops a pan on one toe, bumps one knee, then throws the meal into a car and cooks as it escapes. <reading>TOE—KNEE—CAR—COOK</reading> means the details can wait; <vocabulary>anyway</vocabulary>, get out of the smoky kitchen. とにかく sets side issues aside so the speaker can return to the main point.

contextSentences.ja: とにかく、まず話を聞いてください。
contextSentences.en: Anyway, please hear me out first.

contextSentences.ja: 理由はあとで説明するから、とにかく今は逃げよう。
contextSentences.en: I'll explain why later; for now, let's just get out of here.

contextSentences.ja: この店はとにかく量が多い。
contextSentences.en: This restaurant serves really large portions.

words.meaningMnemonic: A deer 鹿（しか）stands in a rice field 田（た）and stamps a witness statement CERTIFIED. That exact pair, <reading>田（た）—鹿（しか）</reading>, makes you <vocabulary>certain</vocabulary>—or at least say “if I remember correctly.” As an adverb, たしか often signals confident but fallible memory.

contextSentences.ja: たしか、集合は九時だったと思います。
contextSentences.en: If I remember correctly, we were supposed to meet at nine.

contextSentences.ja: たしかな情報が入るまで発表を待ちましょう。
contextSentences.en: Let's wait to make an announcement until we have reliable information.

words.meaningMnemonic: A defeated knight raises one cardboard sword and begs to attack just once more: <reading>攻めて（せめて）</reading>! He cannot win, but asks for <vocabulary>at least</vocabulary> one final swing. せめて marks the minimum outcome the speaker still hopes for.

contextSentences.ja: せめて名前だけでも教えてください。
contextSentences.en: Please tell me at least your name.

contextSentences.ja: せめて一時間あれば、最後まで仕上げられるのに。
contextSentences.en: If only I had at least an hour, I could finish it.

contextSentences.ja: 結果は変わらなくても、せめて謝ってほしい。
contextSentences.en: Even if it won't change the outcome, I at least want an apology.

words.meaningMnemonic: One person ひと plants a flag labeled FIRST まず halfway up a mountain, then calls a temporary halt. The two signs flash <reading>ひと—まず</reading>: this camp is good enough <vocabulary>for now</vocabulary>. ひとまず describes a provisional pause or solution, not a final conclusion.

contextSentences.ja: ひとまずここで休憩しましょう。
contextSentences.en: For now, let's take a break here.

contextSentences.ja: 水漏れの問題はひとまず解決した。
contextSentences.en: The leak has been dealt with for the time being.

words.meaningMnemonic: A lump of dough predicts the oven will burn it no matter which tray it chooses. Its <reading>DOUGH—SAY</reading> prophecy declares the outcome fixed <vocabulary>anyway</vocabulary>, so it jumps onto the nearest tray. どうせ often carries resignation, though どうせなら can turn that into “if we're doing it anyway.”

contextSentences.ja: どうせ行くなら、早く出よう。
contextSentences.en: If we're going anyway, let's leave early.

contextSentences.ja: どうせ私が何を言っても、彼は聞かない。
contextSentences.en: No matter what I say, he isn't going to listen.

words.meaningMnemonic: Whatever 何（なに）happens, the white castle 白（しろ）must open before the festival. Its gates spell <reading>なに—白（しろ）</reading>: <vocabulary>at any rate</vocabulary>, the crowd is already waiting; <vocabulary>after all</vocabulary>, it is the only castle in town. なにしろ commonly introduces the overriding reason for what follows.

contextSentences.ja: なにしろ初めてなので、少し緊張しています。
contextSentences.en: After all, it's my first time, so I'm a little nervous.

contextSentences.ja: なにしろ荷物が多くて、一人では運べません。
contextSentences.en: The thing is, there is so much luggage that I can't carry it alone.

words.meaningMnemonic: A friend eyes your umbrella and whispers, “もし…貸して（かして）?”—“If… lend it to me?” That tentative <reading>もし—貸して</reading> makes you wonder: <vocabulary>perhaps</vocabulary> she forgot hers, <vocabulary>by any chance</vocabulary>? もしかして introduces a guess, often in a question.

contextSentences.ja: もしかして、道に迷いましたか。
contextSentences.en: Did you get lost, by any chance?

contextSentences.ja: もしかして、鍵を会社に忘れたかもしれない。
contextSentences.en: Maybe I left my keys at the office.

words.meaningMnemonic: A flour trail crosses the yard while cheerleaders point and shout <reading>DOUGH—YEAH—RAH!</reading> The detective studies the clues and says, “<vocabulary>It seems</vocabulary> the runaway dough escaped this way.” どうやら presents a conclusion based on signs rather than direct certainty.

contextSentences.ja: どうやら電車が遅れているようです。
contextSentences.en: Apparently, the train is running late.

contextSentences.ja: 足跡を見ると、どうやら犬が庭に入ったらしい。
contextSentences.en: Judging by the tracks, it seems a dog got into the yard.

words.meaningMnemonic: An acrobat hears <reading>HO—BOW!</reading> and bends until her nose is one millimeter from her knees. The bow is <vocabulary>almost</vocabulary>, but not completely, finished. ほぼ can mean nearly all of something or approximately a number.

contextSentences.ja: 準備はほぼ終わりました。
contextSentences.en: The preparations are almost finished.

contextSentences.ja: 駅までは歩いてほぼ十分です。
contextSentences.en: It's about a ten-minute walk to the station.

contextSentences.ja: 参加者のほぼ半数が初参加だった。
contextSentences.en: Almost half of the participants were attending for the first time.

packs.title: Feelings You Can Hear
packs.description: Everyday mimetic words for excitement, nerves, irritation, disappointment, relief, and suspense.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two woks bounce toward each other before a cooking contest, clanging <reading>WOK—WOK!</reading> The cooks can hardly wait; everyone is <vocabulary>excited</vocabulary> to see what flies out. わくわく describes eager anticipation and can pair with する.

contextSentences.ja: 旅行の前日はいつもわくわくする。
contextSentences.en: I always feel excited the day before a trip.

contextSentences.ja: 子どもたちはプレゼントをわくわくしながら開けた。
contextSentences.en: The children excitedly opened their presents.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two knees paint cheerful faces on their caps and knock together: <reading>KNEE—CO, KNEE—CO!</reading> Both faces keep <vocabulary>smiling</vocabulary> warmly no matter how often they bump. にこにこ describes an openly friendly, happy smile and can pair with する.

contextSentences.ja: 子どもはプレゼントを見てにこにこしていた。
contextSentences.en: The child was smiling when they saw the present.

contextSentences.ja: 祖母は赤ちゃんを見ながら、にこにこ笑った。
contextSentences.en: My grandmother smiled cheerfully as she looked at the baby.

words.meaningMnemonic: A broken arena sign flashes the letter E while its cheer squad answers RAH, then the loop starts again: <reading>E—RAH, E—RAH!</reading> The endless light and racket leave everyone visibly <vocabulary>irritated</vocabulary>. いらいらする is the common pattern for becoming or feeling annoyed.

contextSentences.ja: 渋滞でなかなか進まず、いらいらした。
contextSentences.en: I got irritated because the traffic barely moved.

contextSentences.ja: 彼の失礼な言い方にいらいらする。
contextSentences.en: The rude way he speaks irritates me.

words.meaningMnemonic: A monkey discovers two keys and leaps from branch to branch shouting <reading>OOH—KEY! OOH—KEY!</reading> Its whole body bounces <vocabulary>cheerfully</vocabulary>, plainly <vocabulary>in high spirits</vocabulary>. うきうき suggests buoyant happiness about something pleasant.

contextSentences.ja: 新しい服を着て、うきうきしながら出かけた。
contextSentences.en: I went out in high spirits wearing my new clothes.

contextSentences.ja: 明日から休みだと思うと、気分がうきうきする。
contextSentences.en: Knowing that my break starts tomorrow puts me in a cheerful mood.

words.meaningMnemonic: You gasp GACK, then carry home the huge gift box—only to find it empty. The clipped sounds collide in <reading>GACK—CARRY</reading>, and your shoulders drop because you are <vocabulary>disappointed</vocabulary>. がっかりする is used when hopes or expectations collapse.

contextSentences.ja: 試合が中止になって、みんながっかりした。
contextSentences.en: Everyone was disappointed when the game was canceled.

contextSentences.ja: 悪い結果でも、あまりがっかりしないでね。
contextSentences.en: Even if the result is bad, don't be too discouraged.

words.meaningMnemonic: A BIC-pen courier bursts from a parcel and fires the pen into your hand: <reading>BIC—COURIER!</reading> The impossible delivery leaves you completely <vocabulary>startled</vocabulary>. びっくりする covers surprise from good, bad, or merely unexpected events.

contextSentences.ja: 後ろから名前を呼ばれてびっくりした。
contextSentences.en: I was startled when someone called my name from behind.

contextSentences.ja: ホテルの値段の高さにびっくりした。
contextSentences.en: I was surprised by how expensive the hotel was.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two camphor trees 楠 hide birds in their leaves, and each tree begins to laugh: <reading>楠（くす）—楠（くす）</reading>. The secret little sounds turn into a suppressed <vocabulary>giggle</vocabulary>. くすくす describes quiet, repeated chuckling rather than loud laughter.

contextSentences.ja: 後ろの席からくすくす笑う声が聞こえた。
contextSentences.en: I heard quiet giggling from the back row.

contextSentences.ja: 二人は顔を見合わせてくすくす笑った。
contextSentences.en: The two of them looked at each other and giggled.

words.meaningMnemonic: A kettle spills onto your foot, but thick slippers protect it; you gasp <reading>HOT—TOE!</reading> and then laugh. Knowing your toe is safe leaves you deeply <vocabulary>relieved</vocabulary>. ほっとする means to feel relief after tension or worry ends.

contextSentences.ja: 無事だと聞いて、ほっとしました。
contextSentences.en: I was relieved to hear that all was well.

contextSentences.ja: 試験が終わって、やっとほっと一息つけた。
contextSentences.en: Once the exam was over, I could finally breathe a sigh of relief.

words.meaningMnemonic: A timid baker drops the same lump of dough twice whenever the head chef looks over: “Oh, dough! Oh, dough!” Each anxious <reading>OH—DOUGH, OH—DOUGH</reading> comes with another flinch, so the baker works <vocabulary>nervously</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>timidly</vocabulary>. おどおど describes visibly hesitant, fearful behavior, often in おどおどする or おどおどした.

contextSentences.ja: 彼は先生の前でおどおどしていた。
contextSentences.en: He acted nervously in front of the teacher.

contextSentences.ja: 店員に話しかけられ、彼女はおどおどした声で答えた。
contextSentences.en: When the clerk spoke to her, she answered in a timid voice.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two giant stomachs 腹 bounce on a fraying tightrope above the crowd: <reading>腹（はら）—腹（はら）</reading>. Everyone watches <vocabulary>anxiously</vocabulary> as each belly wobbles over the drop. はらはら is the nervous feeling of watching an uncertain, risky outcome.

contextSentences.ja: 最後までどちらが勝つか分からず、はらはらした。
contextSentences.en: I was on edge because I couldn't tell who would win until the end.

contextSentences.ja: 子どもが高い塀の上を歩くのを見て、はらはらした。
contextSentences.en: Watching the child walk along the high wall made me nervous.

contextSentences.ja: このドラマは毎回はらはらする展開になる。
contextSentences.en: Every episode of this drama takes a suspenseful turn.

packs.title: How Things Move
packs.description: Mimetic adverbs for relaxed, smooth, rapid, gentle, unsteady, circular, and last-second movement.

words.meaningMnemonic: The runner in last place ビリ stops mid-race, drinks 飲ん（のん）a whole pot of tea, and lies in the grass: <reading>飲ん（のん）—ビリ</reading>. With no interest in catching up, he spends the afternoon <vocabulary>at leisure</vocabulary>. のんびりする means to relax or take it easy without pressure.

contextSentences.ja: 休日は家でのんびり過ごしたい。
contextSentences.en: I want to spend my day off relaxing at home.

contextSentences.ja: 急がずに、海辺をのんびり歩いた。
contextSentences.en: I took a leisurely walk along the beach without rushing.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two bras sway from a wandering clothesline, chanting <reading>BRA—BRA</reading> as it begins to <vocabulary>stroll aimlessly</vocabulary> through town. Both the laundry and the line dangle wherever the wind leads. ぶらぶら can describe either loose swinging or an unhurried wander.

contextSentences.ja: 時間があったので、駅の周りをぶらぶらした。
contextSentences.en: I had time, so I wandered around the station.

contextSentences.ja: 切れたひもがかばんからぶらぶら下がっている。
contextSentences.en: A broken strap is dangling from the bag.

words.meaningMnemonic: A skeleton adds one bone 骨 to a tower every morning and one more every night: <reading>骨（こつ）—骨（こつ）</reading>. The tower rises <vocabulary>steadily</vocabulary> through patient, diligent work. こつこつ describes sustained small efforts rather than one dramatic burst.

contextSentences.ja: 毎日こつこつ勉強を続けている。
contextSentences.en: I keep studying diligently every day.

contextSentences.ja: 少ない金額でも、毎月こつこつ貯金している。
contextSentences.en: Even though it's only a small amount, I steadily save money every month.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two actual goons grab a rope and chant <reading>GOON—GOON</reading> as they haul a tiny plant upward like a rocket. It grows <vocabulary>rapidly</vocabulary>, gaining height by leaps and bounds. ぐんぐん emphasizes strong, steady progress rather than one sudden jump.

contextSentences.ja: この一年で、子どもたちは背がぐんぐん伸びた。
contextSentences.en: Over the past year, the children shot up in height.

contextSentences.ja: 午後になると気温がぐんぐん上がった。
contextSentences.en: The temperature climbed rapidly in the afternoon.

contextSentences.ja: 練習を始めてから、彼女の記録はぐんぐん伸びている。
contextSentences.en: Since she began practicing, her results have improved by leaps and bounds.

words.meaningMnemonic: A noisy sot notices a sleeping mouse, balances a glass on one toe, and whispers <reading>SOT—TOE</reading> as the two t sounds meet. For once, he lowers the glass <vocabulary>gently</vocabulary> and quietly enough that the mouse never wakes. そっと describes careful, unobtrusive action and can also mean leaving something alone.

contextSentences.ja: 赤ちゃんを起こさないように、ドアをそっと閉めた。
contextSentences.en: I gently closed the door so I wouldn't wake the baby.

contextSentences.ja: 会議の途中で、彼は部屋をそっと抜け出した。
contextSentences.en: He quietly slipped out of the room during the meeting.

words.meaningMnemonic: A jittery toy hears <reading>JIT—TOE!</reading> and freezes while balancing on one toe. It stays perfectly <vocabulary>still</vocabulary>, staring intently ahead. じっと can describe motionless waiting, a fixed gaze, or patient endurance.

contextSentences.ja: 猫は窓の外をじっと見ていた。
contextSentences.en: The cat stared intently out the window.

contextSentences.ja: 写真を撮る間、じっとしていてください。
contextSentences.en: Please keep still while I take the picture.

contextSentences.ja: 彼は何も言わず、痛みをじっとこらえた。
contextSentences.en: Without saying anything, he patiently endured the pain.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two loose flags stagger down the street crying <reading>FLA—FLA</reading> as their poles bend from side to side. They can move only <vocabulary>unsteadily</vocabulary>. ふらふら often describes shaky walking from dizziness or exhaustion, and can also describe wavering decisions.

contextSentences.ja: 熱があって、立つとふらふらする。
contextSentences.en: I have a fever and feel unsteady when I stand.

contextSentences.ja: 彼は疲れた足でふらふら歩いていた。
contextSentences.en: He was staggering along on tired legs.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two gurus climb onto a teacup ride and chant <reading>GURU—GURU</reading> while it spins faster. Their robes wrap <vocabulary>round and round</vocabulary> the center pole. ぐるぐる describes repeated circular movement or something wound around another object.

contextSentences.ja: 子どもが同じ場所をぐるぐる回っている。
contextSentences.en: The child is going round and round in the same spot.

contextSentences.ja: 長いマフラーを首にぐるぐる巻いた。
contextSentences.en: I wrapped the long scarf around my neck several times.

contextSentences.ja: 考えが頭の中をぐるぐる巡って、眠れなかった。
contextSentences.en: Thoughts kept circling in my head, and I couldn't sleep.

words.meaningMnemonic: A hungry chicken attacks an empty bowl: <reading>PECK—OH, PECK—OH!</reading> Every peck finds nothing, so it grows more <vocabulary>starving</vocabulary>. お腹がぺこぺこ is a casual, vivid way to say your stomach is completely empty.

contextSentences.ja: 朝から何も食べていなくて、お腹がぺこぺこだ。
contextSentences.en: I haven't eaten since morning, so I'm starving.

contextSentences.ja: 運動したら、お腹がぺこぺこになった。
contextSentences.en: After exercising, I became ravenously hungry.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two rusty gears grind <reading>GEAR-Y—GEAR-Y</reading> and catch one final tooth before the clock stops. The machine finishes <vocabulary>just barely</vocabulary>, at the absolute limit. ぎりぎり is used for narrow margins in time, space, rules, or ability.

contextSentences.ja: 締め切りぎりぎりにレポートを出した。
contextSentences.en: I submitted the report right at the deadline.

contextSentences.ja: この箱は棚にぎりぎり入る大きさだ。
contextSentences.en: This box is just small enough to fit on the shelf.

packs.title: Food Texture in Every Bite
packs.description: Sound-symbolic texture words for chewy, crunchy, slick, flowing, sticky, rough, crisp, and melting foods.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two pieces of mochi stretch across the room and bounce back together with a <reading>MOCHI—MOCHI</reading> snap. That elastic pull is unmistakably <vocabulary>chewy</vocabulary> and springy. もちもち is especially common for pleasantly elastic foods such as rice cakes, bread, and noodles.

contextSentences.ja: このパンは中がもちもちしている。
contextSentences.en: The inside of this bread is pleasantly chewy.

contextSentences.ja: 米粉を使うと、麺がもちもちした食感になる。
contextSentences.en: Using rice flour gives the noodles a springy texture.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two sacks of crackers tumble down the stairs, breaking open with <reading>SACK—SACK</reading> crunches. Every bite is dry, light, and <vocabulary>crisp</vocabulary>. さくさく often praises flaky pastries, fried coatings, or efficient progress through a task.

contextSentences.ja: 揚げたてのコロッケは衣がさくさくだ。
contextSentences.en: The coating on the freshly fried croquette is crisp.

contextSentences.ja: 天ぷらの衣をさくさくにするため、冷たい水を使った。
contextSentences.en: I used cold water to make the tempura batter crisp.

words.meaningMnemonic: A knight uses two potato chips to parry arrows, shouting <reading>PARRY—PARRY!</reading> Each shield cracks because it is so thin and <vocabulary>crispy</vocabulary>. ぱりぱり suits brittle foods, tearing paper, and other sharp crackling sounds.

contextSentences.ja: 焼きのりがぱりぱりしていておいしい。
contextSentences.en: The toasted seaweed is crispy and delicious.

contextSentences.ja: 包装紙を丸めると、ぱりぱりと音がした。
contextSentences.en: The wrapping paper crackled when I crumpled it.

words.meaningMnemonic: A squirrel orders two porters to <reading>CARRY—CARRY</reading> mountains of hard crackers into its tree. It crunches them noisily, then snaps <vocabulary>irritably</vocabulary> when one is missing. かりかり can describe a hard crunchy texture or an edgy, bad-tempered mood.

contextSentences.ja: ベーコンをかりかりになるまで焼いた。
contextSentences.en: I cooked the bacon until it was crispy.

contextSentences.ja: 待たされると、父はすぐかりかりする。
contextSentences.en: My father gets irritated quickly when he is kept waiting.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two polished tools slide from a workbench, ringing <reading>TOOL—TOOL</reading> as nobody can grip them. Their surfaces are perfectly <vocabulary>smooth</vocabulary> and slippery. つるつる also evokes noodles slipping easily into the mouth.

contextSentences.ja: この石は水で磨かれてつるつるだ。
contextSentences.en: This stone has been polished smooth by the water.

contextSentences.ja: 道が凍ってつるつるなので、転ばないように気をつけて。
contextSentences.en: The road is icy and slippery, so be careful not to fall.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two plates 皿 tip together and release rivers of silky hair: <reading>皿（さら）—皿（さら）</reading>. Nothing clumps or catches; every strand becomes <vocabulary>silky smooth</vocabulary> and flows freely. さらさら commonly describes smooth dry hair, fine powder, or a gently flowing stream.

contextSentences.ja: このシャンプーを使うと髪がさらさらになる。
contextSentences.en: This shampoo makes my hair silky smooth.

contextSentences.ja: 乾いた砂が指の間からさらさら落ちた。
contextSentences.en: Dry sand flowed smoothly between my fingers.

contextSentences.ja: 小川の水がさらさらと流れている。
contextSentences.en: The stream is flowing with a soft, gentle sound.

words.meaningMnemonic: A wall covered in BETA labels grabs your sleeves whenever you pass: <reading>BETA—BETA</reading>. The labels are horribly <vocabulary>sticky</vocabulary> and cling to everything. べたべた can describe a tacky surface or people being excessively physically affectionate.

contextSentences.ja: ジュースをこぼして、床がべたべたする。
contextSentences.en: I spilled juice, and the floor is sticky.

contextSentences.ja: 汗でシャツが背中にべたべた張りつく。
contextSentences.en: My shirt sticks to my back because of the sweat.

contextSentences.ja: 人前でそんなにべたべたするのはやめて。
contextSentences.en: Stop acting so clingy in public.

words.meaningMnemonic: A czar rubs two sheets of sandpaper together and commands, <reading>CZAR—A, CZAR—A!</reading> The scraping surface feels <vocabulary>rough</vocabulary> and gritty under every fingertip. ざらざら describes coarse textures and can also describe a rough voice.

contextSentences.ja: 砂が付いて、タオルがざらざらしている。
contextSentences.en: Sand is stuck to the towel, so it feels gritty.

contextSentences.ja: この紙は表面がざらざらしていて、鉛筆で描きやすい。
contextSentences.en: This paper has a rough surface that is easy to draw on with a pencil.

words.meaningMnemonic: A bundle of celery shakes across the cutting board chanting <reading>SHAKY—SHAKY</reading>. Every slice snaps cleanly because the vegetables are fresh and <vocabulary>crisp</vocabulary>. しゃきしゃき often describes the firm crunch of raw vegetables and can also suggest brisk, precise behavior.

contextSentences.ja: このサラダのレタスはしゃきしゃきしている。
contextSentences.en: The lettuce in this salad is crisp.

contextSentences.ja: れんこんをさっと炒めて、しゃきしゃきした食感を残した。
contextSentences.en: I stir-fried the lotus root briefly so it kept its crisp texture.

words.meaningMnemonic: A cook tries to throw melted cheese, yelling <reading>THROW—THROW</reading>, but it oozes from the spoon in one slow ribbon. The cheese is <vocabulary>thick and runny</vocabulary>, almost meltingly soft. とろとろ also describes gentle simmering or someone beginning to doze.

contextSentences.ja: 卵を半熟にして、黄身をとろとろにした。
contextSentences.en: I soft-cooked the egg so the yolk was runny.

contextSentences.ja: 野菜をとろとろになるまで弱火で煮込んだ。
contextSentences.en: I simmered the vegetables over low heat until they were meltingly soft.

packs.title: Weather You Can Feel
packs.description: Vivid everyday words for warmth, humidity, chill, clouds, rain, breeze, soaking, and clear dry weather.

words.meaningMnemonic: A cat pokes a heater twice—<reading>POKE-A—POKE-A</reading>—then curls up in the sunbeam it releases. The room becomes <vocabulary>pleasantly warm</vocabulary>, never scorching. ぽかぽか often describes sunshine, a room, or a comfortably warmed body.

contextSentences.ja: 今日はぽかぽかした陽気で、上着はいらない。
contextSentences.en: It's pleasantly warm today, so I don't need a jacket.

contextSentences.ja: 温かいスープを飲むと、体がぽかぽかしてきた。
contextSentences.en: After drinking the warm soup, my body began to feel nice and warm.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two crowded gyms drip condensation while their doors groan <reading>GYM—EH, GYM—EH</reading>. The air and towels stay unpleasantly <vocabulary>damp</vocabulary> and humid. じめじめ can describe clammy weather or, figuratively, a gloomy atmosphere.

contextSentences.ja: 梅雨は部屋の中までじめじめする。
contextSentences.en: During the rainy season, even the inside of the room feels damp.

contextSentences.ja: じめじめした押し入れに、かびが生えてしまった。
contextSentences.en: Mold grew in the damp closet.

words.meaningMnemonic: The summer air turns bread into mush, and each step squelches <reading>MUSHY—MUSHY</reading>. Heat and moisture combine into oppressively <vocabulary>muggy</vocabulary> weather. むしむし specifically emphasizes an uncomfortable mix of heat and humidity.

contextSentences.ja: 今夜はむしむしして寝苦しい。
contextSentences.en: It's muggy tonight and hard to sleep.

contextSentences.ja: 雨が上がったあと、電車の中はむしむししていた。
contextSentences.en: After the rain stopped, it felt hot and humid inside the train.

words.meaningMnemonic: A store product 品 turns out to be a spear 槍 pulled straight from a freezer: <reading>品（ひん）—槍（やり）</reading>. Its metal point feels suddenly <vocabulary>cool</vocabulary>, pleasantly chilly rather than painfully cold. ひんやり often describes the immediate sensation of a cool object, room, or breeze.

contextSentences.ja: 洞窟の中はひんやりしていた。
contextSentences.en: It was pleasantly cool inside the cave.

contextSentences.ja: 冷蔵庫から出した桃がひんやり冷たい。
contextSentences.en: The peach from the refrigerator feels refreshingly cold.

words.meaningMnemonic: A giant rice bowl 丼 leans 寄り toward the window and blocks every ray of sun: <reading>丼（どん）—寄り（より）</reading>. The room turns <vocabulary>overcast</vocabulary> and gloomy before a drop even falls. どんより can describe a heavy gray sky or dull, lifeless eyes and mood.

contextSentences.ja: 朝から空がどんより曇っている。
contextSentences.en: The sky has been heavily overcast since morning.

contextSentences.ja: 失敗のことを考えると、気分がどんよりする。
contextSentences.en: Thinking about the failure puts me in a gloomy mood.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two czars overturn storm barrels above a metal roof, each title drawn out in the roar: <reading>CZAAAR—CZAAAR!</reading> The rain is <vocabulary>pouring</vocabulary> so hard that the street vanishes. ざあざあ evokes heavy rain or a large volume of rushing water, not a light shower.

contextSentences.ja: 外では雨がざあざあ降っている。
contextSentences.en: Rain is pouring down outside.

contextSentences.ja: 雨がざあざあ降ってきたので、近くの店で雨宿りした。
contextSentences.en: When the rain began pouring, I took shelter in a nearby shop.

words.meaningMnemonic: Tiny drops land on a bedsheet and quietly murmur <reading>SHEET—OH, SHEET—OH</reading>. It keeps <vocabulary>drizzling</vocabulary> in a soft, steady rhythm. しとしと suggests steady, quiet rain rather than a brief sprinkle or downpour.

contextSentences.ja: 午後から雨がしとしと降り続いた。
contextSentences.en: A gentle rain kept falling from the afternoon onward.

contextSentences.ja: しとしと降る雨の中を、傘を差して歩いた。
contextSentences.en: I walked through the gentle rain under an umbrella.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two bees take turns showing their rain-heavy wings—<reading>BEE—SHOW, BEE—SHOW</reading>—and fling water across your coat. Streams run from every pocket; you are completely <vocabulary>soaked</vocabulary>. びしょびしょ describes something thoroughly wet, stronger than merely damp.

contextSentences.ja: 傘を忘れて、服がびしょびしょになった。
contextSentences.en: I forgot my umbrella, and my clothes got soaked.

contextSentences.ja: 犬が体を振って、床をびしょびしょにした。
contextSentences.en: The dog shook itself and left the floor sopping wet.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two yo-yos hang from a tree and sway <reading>SO—YO, SO—YO</reading> without completing a single spin. A pleasant breeze is <vocabulary>gently blowing</vocabulary> through their strings. そよそよ is used mainly for a light, pleasant wind.

contextSentences.ja: 窓から涼しい風がそよそよ入ってくる。
contextSentences.en: A cool breeze is gently coming through the window.

contextSentences.ja: 川辺では、風がそよそよと柳の葉を揺らしていた。
contextSentences.en: A gentle breeze was stirring the willow leaves by the river.

words.meaningMnemonic: A rat hangs laundry across a car, tests the hot hood with one toe, and cries <reading>CAR—RAT—TOE!</reading> The sky has turned <vocabulary>bright and clear</vocabulary>, and every shirt dries cleanly. からっと can praise clear dry weather, nicely dried laundry, or crisp frying.

contextSentences.ja: 雨の翌日はからっと晴れた。
contextSentences.en: The day after the rain was bright and clear.

contextSentences.ja: 洗濯物がからっと乾いて気持ちいい。
contextSentences.en: The laundry dried thoroughly and feels wonderfully fresh.

packs.title: Body Signals
packs.description: Common kana spellings for sneezing, hiccups, dizziness, swelling, numbness, skin marks, and body parts.

words.meaningMnemonic: A pigeon coos into a chamois cloth, inhales its dust, and explodes: <reading>COO—SHAMMY!</reading> Feathers fly with one enormous <vocabulary>sneeze</vocabulary>. くしゃみ is the noun; くしゃみをする means to sneeze.

contextSentences.ja: 花粉のせいでくしゃみが止まらない。
contextSentences.en: I can't stop sneezing because of the pollen.

contextSentences.ja: ほこりを吸い込んだら、大きなくしゃみが出た。
contextSentences.en: I breathed in some dust and let out a big sneeze.

words.meaningMnemonic: A tiny shack jerks upward at regular intervals and squeaks <reading>SHACK—REE!</reading> Each sudden jump is another stubborn <vocabulary>hiccup</vocabulary>. しゃっくりが出る means to get hiccups, while しゃっくりが止まる means they stop.

contextSentences.ja: 水を飲んだらしゃっくりが止まった。
contextSentences.en: My hiccups stopped after I drank water.

contextSentences.ja: 食事の途中で急にしゃっくりが出始めた。
contextSentences.en: I suddenly started hiccuping in the middle of the meal.

words.meaningMnemonic: A funhouse mirror droops and mutters <reading>MEH—MY!</reading> as its own reflection spins off the wall. You cannot focus either because a wave of <vocabulary>dizziness</vocabulary> has hit. めまいがする is the usual way to say that you feel dizzy.

contextSentences.ja: 急に立ち上がったら、めまいがした。
contextSentences.en: I felt dizzy when I stood up suddenly.

contextSentences.ja: 朝からめまいが続いているので、病院に行くことにした。
contextSentences.en: I've been dizzy since this morning, so I decided to go to the hospital.

words.meaningMnemonic: A cow steps on your boots, then coos at you—<reading>MOO—COO—ME</reading>—while your feet balloon over the laces. The exaggerated puffiness makes <vocabulary>swelling</vocabulary> impossible to miss. むくみ commonly refers to fluid-related swelling in the face, hands, or legs.

contextSentences.ja: 長時間飛行機に乗った後、足にむくみが出た。
contextSentences.en: My legs became swollen after the long flight.

contextSentences.ja: 朝起きると、顔のむくみが気になった。
contextSentences.en: When I woke up, I noticed that my face looked puffy.

words.meaningMnemonic: A bee fires a pale ray at her arm: <reading>SHE—BEE—RAY!</reading> The arm goes dead and prickly with <vocabulary>numbness</vocabulary>. しびれ can be loss of sensation or pins and needles; しびれる means to become numb.

contextSentences.ja: 正座をしていたら、足にしびれがきた。
contextSentences.en: My legs went numb after I sat in seiza.

contextSentences.ja: 指のしびれがなかなか取れない。
contextSentences.en: The numbness in my fingers isn't going away.

words.meaningMnemonic: A hawk rows a boat with one wing, chanting <reading>HAWK—ROW</reading>; under the other wing is one unmistakable dark dot. That little spot is a <vocabulary>mole</vocabulary> or beauty mark. ほくろ refers to a pigmented skin mark, not an animal mole.

contextSentences.ja: 彼は左の頬に小さなほくろがある。
contextSentences.en: He has a small mole on his left cheek.

contextSentences.ja: 鏡を見ると、鼻の横に新しいほくろができていた。
contextSentences.en: When I looked in the mirror, I noticed a new mole beside my nose.

words.meaningMnemonic: A bee steals the key tied to your knee, then leaves a bright red bump as it escapes: <reading>KNEE—KEY—BEE!</reading> The bump becomes one angry <vocabulary>pimple</vocabulary>. にきび can mean an individual pimple or acne collectively.

contextSentences.ja: 寝不足が続くと、にきびができやすい。
contextSentences.en: I tend to get pimples when I don't sleep enough.

contextSentences.ja: 額にできたにきびが少し痛い。
contextSentences.en: The pimple on my forehead hurts a little.

words.meaningMnemonic: He bangs his arm on the table and yelps <reading>HE—GEE!</reading> while clutching the sharp joint in the middle. The injured joint is his <vocabulary>elbow</vocabulary>. ひじ is the elbow; ひざ, with a different final sound, is the knee.

contextSentences.ja: 机にひじをぶつけてしまった。
contextSentences.en: I accidentally hit my elbow on the desk.

contextSentences.ja: ひじを曲げると痛いので、重い物を持てない。
contextSentences.en: My elbow hurts when I bend it, so I can't lift anything heavy.

words.meaningMnemonic: You stumble aboard a ship and strike the deck headfirst: <reading>OH—DECK—OH!</reading> A cartoon bump rises on your <vocabulary>forehead</vocabulary>. おでこ is a familiar everyday word; 額 is the more neutral lexical alternative.

contextSentences.ja: 子どものおでこに手を当てて熱を確かめた。
contextSentences.en: I put my hand on the child's forehead to check for a fever.

contextSentences.ja: 低い棚におでこをぶつけた。
contextSentences.en: I bumped my forehead on a low shelf.

words.meaningMnemonic: Ma tries to balance a pig 豚（ぶた）above your eye, and the pig gently pulls the curtain shut. The exact pair <reading>MA—豚（ぶた）</reading> lands on your <vocabulary>eyelid</vocabulary>. まぶた is the movable fold that opens and closes over the eye.

contextSentences.ja: 眠くて、まぶたが重くなってきた。
contextSentences.en: I'm sleepy, and my eyelids are getting heavy.

contextSentences.ja: 朝起きたら、片方のまぶたが腫れていた。
contextSentences.en: When I woke up, one of my eyelids was swollen.

packs.title: Work & Study Desk
packs.description: Core office and school loanwords for meetings, plans, projects, tests, reports, copies, and written notes.

words.meaningMnemonic: An entire <reading>OFFICE</reading> folds into a briefcase, desks and all, then unfolds wherever work begins. The portable room is still an <vocabulary>office</vocabulary>. オフィス usually evokes a modern workplace; 事務所 is another common word for an office or agency.

contextSentences.ja: 新しいオフィスは駅から近い。
contextSentences.en: The new office is close to the station.

contextSentences.ja: 今日は自宅ではなく、オフィスで働きます。
contextSentences.en: Today I'll work at the office rather than from home.

words.meaningMnemonic: Every chair in the building races to the middle and announces a <reading>MEETING</reading>. Once the chairs form a circle, the <vocabulary>meeting</vocabulary> can begin. ミーティング often suggests a practical team discussion; 会議 can sound more formal or decision-oriented.

contextSentences.ja: 午後三時からチームのミーティングがあります。
contextSentences.en: We have a team meeting at three this afternoon.

contextSentences.ja: 海外の同僚とオンラインでミーティングを行った。
contextSentences.en: I held an online meeting with colleagues overseas.

words.readingMap: ミ・ー・ティ・ン・グ

words.meaningMnemonic: A giant <reading>SCHEDULE</reading> unrolls across the floor and traps anyone who misses an appointment. Every square records the <vocabulary>schedule</vocabulary> for the week. スケジュールを立てる means to make a schedule, while 調整する means to adjust one.

contextSentences.ja: 来週のスケジュールを確認してください。
contextSentences.en: Please check next week's schedule.

contextSentences.ja: 出張のスケジュールが急に変更になった。
contextSentences.en: The business trip schedule changed suddenly.

contextSentences.ja: 今月はスケジュールが詰まっていて、休みが取れない。
contextSentences.en: My schedule is packed this month, so I can't take any time off.

words.readingMap: ス・ケ・ジュ・ー・ル

words.meaningMnemonic: A projector fires tasks, deadlines, and teammates onto one enormous board labeled <reading>PROJECT</reading>. All those coordinated pieces belong to a single <vocabulary>project</vocabulary>. プロジェクト usually means an organized undertaking with a defined goal, especially at work or in research.

contextSentences.ja: 新しいプロジェクトに参加することになった。
contextSentences.en: I'm going to take part in a new project.

contextSentences.ja: 予算不足でプロジェクトが一時中断した。
contextSentences.en: The project was temporarily suspended because of a lack of funding.

words.readingMap: プ・ロ・ジェ・ク・ト

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>TEAM</reading> stitches all its jerseys into one bridge so nobody can cross alone. Cooperation turns the group into a real <vocabulary>team</vocabulary>. チーム applies to sports, work, games, and other groups acting toward a shared goal.

contextSentences.ja: この仕事は五人のチームで進めます。
contextSentences.en: A five-person team will carry out this work.

contextSentences.ja: 決勝では強いチームと対戦する。
contextSentences.en: We'll face a strong team in the final.

words.meaningMnemonic: A runaway <reading>PEN</reading> signs every blank page, then draws bars around itself when caught. Even inside its ink prison, the <vocabulary>pen</vocabulary> keeps writing. ペン is the general word for an ink pen; 鉛筆 is specifically a pencil.

contextSentences.ja: この書類は黒いペンで書いてください。
contextSentences.en: Please fill out this document with a black pen.

contextSentences.ja: ペンのインクが切れたので、新しいものに替えた。
contextSentences.en: The pen ran out of ink, so I replaced it with a new one.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>TEST</reading> paper grows eyes and starts examining the student who was meant to examine it. Passing its questions is the only way to finish the <vocabulary>test</vocabulary>. テスト can be a school exam or a trial of performance; 試験 often sounds more formal.

contextSentences.ja: 明日の数学のテストに向けて勉強している。
contextSentences.en: I'm studying for tomorrow's math test.

contextSentences.ja: 新しい機能を公開する前に、十分なテストを行った。
contextSentences.en: We thoroughly tested the new feature before releasing it.

words.meaningMnemonic: A tiny reporter climbs onto your desk and types <reading>REPORT</reading> across forty pages before the deadline bell. The finished stack is your <vocabulary>report</vocabulary> or academic paper. レポートを書く and レポートを提出する are common school and workplace combinations.

contextSentences.ja: 金曜日までにレポートを提出しなければならない。
contextSentences.en: I have to submit the report by Friday.

contextSentences.ja: 実験の結果をレポートにまとめた。
contextSentences.en: I summarized the experiment results in a report.

contextSentences.ja: 記者が現地の様子をレポートした。
contextSentences.en: A reporter covered the situation on location.

words.meaningMnemonic: A copier shouts <reading>COPY!</reading> and produces ten identical versions of your coffee cup along with the document. Each duplicate is a perfect <vocabulary>copy</vocabulary>. コピーする commonly means to photocopy or duplicate data; コピーを取る means to make a copy.

contextSentences.ja: 会議の資料を十部コピーしました。
contextSentences.en: I made ten copies of the meeting materials.

contextSentences.ja: 大切な写真をパソコンにコピーした。
contextSentences.en: I copied the important photos onto my computer.

words.meaningMnemonic: A memory elephant stamps <reading>MEMO</reading> onto a tiny card before the idea can escape. The card becomes a quick written <vocabulary>note</vocabulary>. メモを取る means to take notes; メモする means to jot something down.

contextSentences.ja: 忘れないように電話番号をメモした。
contextSentences.en: I wrote down the phone number so I wouldn't forget it.

contextSentences.ja: 机の上に『牛乳を買う』というメモが置いてあった。
contextSentences.en: There was a note on the desk that said, “Buy milk.”

packs.title: Laundry & Home Care
packs.description: Useful household loanwords for clothes care, hair care, washing, wrapping, floors, and everyday cleaning tools.

words.meaningMnemonic: An <reading>IRON</reading> grows tank treads and flattens a mountain of wrinkled shirts. The steam-powered machine is still a clothes <vocabulary>iron</vocabulary>. アイロンをかける is the standard phrase for ironing clothes.

contextSentences.ja: シャツにアイロンをかけてから着た。
contextSentences.en: I ironed the shirt before putting it on.

contextSentences.ja: アイロンが熱いうちに、ハンカチのしわを伸ばした。
contextSentences.en: While the iron was hot, I pressed the wrinkles out of the handkerchief.

words.meaningMnemonic: A coat <reading>HANGER</reading> sprouts arms and hangs every jacket—including the one you are wearing. The triangular helper is a <vocabulary>clothes hanger</vocabulary>, not an aircraft hangar. ハンガーにかける means to hang clothing on a hanger.

contextSentences.ja: 濡れたシャツをハンガーにかけた。
contextSentences.en: I put the wet shirt on a hanger.

contextSentences.ja: コートは入口にあるハンガーにかけてください。
contextSentences.en: Please hang your coat on the hanger by the entrance.

words.meaningMnemonic: A bottle of <reading>SHAMPOO</reading> erupts into a foam cloud and washes every head in the bathroom at once. The bubbles smell unmistakably of <vocabulary>shampoo</vocabulary>. シャンプーする means to shampoo one's hair; the word usually refers to hair washing rather than body soap.

contextSentences.ja: 旅行用に、小さいボトルのシャンプーを買った。
contextSentences.en: I bought a small bottle of shampoo for traveling.

contextSentences.ja: 海で泳いだあと、髪をよくシャンプーした。
contextSentences.en: After swimming in the sea, I shampooed my hair thoroughly.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>DRYER</reading> blows with hurricane force until wet hair streams horizontally across the room. The roaring machine is a <vocabulary>hair dryer</vocabulary>. Without extra context, ドライヤー most often means a handheld hair dryer.

contextSentences.ja: ドライヤーで髪を乾かした。
contextSentences.en: I dried my hair with a hair dryer.

contextSentences.ja: 夜遅いので、ドライヤーを弱風にして使った。
contextSentences.en: Since it was late at night, I used the hair dryer on a low setting.

words.meaningMnemonic: A giant <reading>BRUSH</reading> marches through the house, scrubbing shoes, hair, and bottles with different bristles. Every attachment is still a kind of <vocabulary>brush</vocabulary>. ブラシ is a broad tool word; the object being cleaned usually makes the type clear.

contextSentences.ja: 柔らかいブラシで靴の汚れを落とした。
contextSentences.en: I removed the dirt from my shoes with a soft brush.

contextSentences.ja: 朝、鏡の前でブラシを使って髪を整えた。
contextSentences.en: In the morning, I used a brush to tidy my hair in front of the mirror.

words.meaningMnemonic: One bucket tips over and becomes a whole marching line of <reading>BUCKETS</reading>. Each <vocabulary>bucket</vocabulary> carries water to the next until the floor is clean. バケツ is an ordinary handled pail used for water, cleaning, gardening, and similar tasks.

contextSentences.ja: バケツに水を入れて庭まで運んだ。
contextSentences.en: I filled a bucket with water and carried it to the garden.

contextSentences.ja: 雨漏りする場所の下にバケツを置いた。
contextSentences.en: I put a bucket under the spot where the roof was leaking.

words.meaningMnemonic: A kitchen <reading>SPONGE</reading> absorbs the whole sink, dishes and faucet included, then squeezes them back out sparkling. The thirsty yellow block is a <vocabulary>sponge</vocabulary>. スポンジ can be a cleaning sponge or sponge cake material, depending on context.

contextSentences.ja: スポンジに洗剤をつけて皿を洗った。
contextSentences.en: I put detergent on a sponge and washed the dishes.

contextSentences.ja: 浴室の壁を新しいスポンジでこすった。
contextSentences.en: I scrubbed the bathroom wall with a new sponge.

words.meaningMnemonic: A roll shouts <reading>WRAP!</reading> and seals the entire refrigerator under one transparent sheet. The clinging film is kitchen <vocabulary>plastic wrap</vocabulary>. In food and household contexts, ラップ normally means cling film; rap music is a separate context-dependent sense.

contextSentences.ja: 残った料理にラップをして冷蔵庫に入れた。
contextSentences.en: I covered the leftover food with plastic wrap and put it in the refrigerator.

contextSentences.ja: ラップを少し緩めてから、レンジで温めた。
contextSentences.en: I loosened the plastic wrap a little before heating it in the microwave.

words.meaningMnemonic: A shopkeeper tries to sell a roll, but it sticks to the counter and he cries <reading>SELL—OH—TAPE!</reading> The l sound flows into OH as the transparent strip becomes <vocabulary>clear adhesive tape</vocabulary>. セロテープ is the ordinary clear stationery tape; ガムテープ is the heavier tape used for packing boxes.

contextSentences.ja: 破れた紙をセロテープで直した。
contextSentences.en: I repaired the torn paper with clear tape.

contextSentences.ja: ポスターの四隅をセロテープで壁に貼った。
contextSentences.en: I taped the four corners of the poster to the wall with clear tape.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>MOP</reading> grows a hundred yarn legs and races across a spill before anyone slips. The many-legged cleaner is still a floor <vocabulary>mop</vocabulary>. モップをかける means to mop a surface.

contextSentences.ja: 閉店後にモップで床を拭いた。
contextSentences.en: After closing, I mopped the floor.

contextSentences.ja: 床に水をこぼしたので、モップを持ってきた。
contextSentences.en: I spilled water on the floor, so I brought over a mop.

packs.title: Around the City
packs.description: Travel and city loanwords for platforms, crowds, guided trips, rentals, facilities, lockers, and motorbikes.

words.meaningMnemonic: A tiny <reading>HOME</reading> with curtains and a chimney sits beside the tracks, but trains stop at its front door. Here the little home marks the <vocabulary>train platform</vocabulary>. ホーム is short for プラットホーム in station contexts; it does not normally mean your house there.

contextSentences.ja: 電車は三番ホームに到着します。
contextSentences.en: The train will arrive at platform three.

contextSentences.ja: ホームの黄色い線の内側でお待ちください。
contextSentences.en: Please wait behind the yellow line on the platform.

words.meaningMnemonic: At eight sharp, an entire crowd yells <reading>RUSH!</reading> and squeezes through one train door like toothpaste. That surge is the morning <vocabulary>rush hour</vocabulary>. ラッシュ can mean any sudden rush, but commuting context usually points to peak crowding.

contextSentences.ja: 朝のラッシュを避けて早く家を出た。
contextSentences.en: I left home early to avoid the morning rush.

contextSentences.ja: 連休の初日は帰省ラッシュが予想されている。
contextSentences.en: Heavy holiday travel is expected on the first day of the long weekend.

words.meaningMnemonic: A glowing <reading>GUIDE</reading> arrow grows legs and leads the tour through every hidden alley. The walking sign is now the group's <vocabulary>tour guide</vocabulary>. ガイド can be a person, a guidebook, or the act of guiding, depending on the construction.

contextSentences.ja: 現地のガイドが町を案内してくれた。
contextSentences.en: A local guide showed us around the town.

contextSentences.ja: 美術館では無料の音声ガイドを借りられる。
contextSentences.en: You can borrow a free audio guide at the museum.

contextSentences.ja: 旅行ガイドを読んで、行きたい店を選んだ。
contextSentences.en: I read a travel guide and chose the shops I wanted to visit.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>TOUR</reading> bus sprouts tiny feet and walks its passengers through five cities without using a road. Every stop belongs to the organized <vocabulary>tour</vocabulary>. ツアー often means a packaged or scheduled trip, including a concert tour.

contextSentences.ja: 週末のバスツアーに申し込みました。
contextSentences.en: I signed up for a weekend bus tour.

contextSentences.ja: 工場を見学するツアーは一時間かかります。
contextSentences.en: The factory tour takes one hour.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>CAMP</reading> tent unfolds itself, lights a fire, and invites the trees to sleep inside. The forest has turned into a <vocabulary>camp</vocabulary>. キャンプする means to go camping; sports teams also use キャンプ for a training camp.

contextSentences.ja: 夏休みに湖の近くでキャンプした。
contextSentences.en: We camped near a lake during summer vacation.

contextSentences.ja: 雨が強くなり、予定より早くキャンプを切り上げた。
contextSentences.en: The rain grew heavier, so we ended our camping trip earlier than planned.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>RENTAL</reading> bicycle carries a giant return clock that rings whenever your time is nearly up. Because it must go back, the bicycle is only a <vocabulary>rental</vocabulary>. レンタル emphasizes borrowing for a fee; レンタルする can mean to rent an item.

contextSentences.ja: 駅前で自転車をレンタルできます。
contextSentences.en: You can rent a bicycle in front of the station.

contextSentences.ja: スキー板のレンタル料金は一日三千円です。
contextSentences.en: Ski rental costs three thousand yen per day.

words.meaningMnemonic: A building marked <reading>CENTER</reading> rolls itself to the exact middle of town and opens a dozen public-service doors. The central facility is the community <vocabulary>center</vocabulary>. センター appears frequently in facility names such as スポーツセンター and サポートセンター.

contextSentences.ja: 市民センターで日本語の教室が開かれている。
contextSentences.en: Japanese classes are held at the community center.

contextSentences.ja: 観光センターで町の地図をもらった。
contextSentences.en: I picked up a map of the town at the tourist information center.

words.meaningMnemonic: A glowing line draws an <reading>AREA</reading> around one part of the city and lifts it like a puzzle piece. Everything inside belongs to that <vocabulary>area</vocabulary> or zone. エリア often marks a service region, designated zone, or part of a larger venue.

contextSentences.ja: このエリアでは無料のWi-Fiが使えます。
contextSentences.en: Free Wi-Fi is available in this area.

contextSentences.ja: 駅の北側は静かな住宅エリアです。
contextSentences.en: The area north of the station is a quiet residential neighborhood.

words.meaningMnemonic: A giant <reading>COIN LOCKER</reading> swallows your suitcase only after a coin opens its metal mouth. The station monster is a <vocabulary>coin-operated locker</vocabulary>. Coin lockers are common at stations and other busy public facilities.

contextSentences.ja: 荷物を駅のコインロッカーに預けた。
contextSentences.en: I left my luggage in a coin locker at the station.

contextSentences.ja: 大きなコインロッカーはすべて使用中だった。
contextSentences.en: All of the large coin lockers were in use.

words.readingMap: コ・イ・ン・ロ・ッ・カ・ー

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>BIKE</reading> roars awake, grows an engine, and leaves every pedal bicycle behind. In this scene—and usually in Japanese—the vehicle is a <vocabulary>motorcycle</vocabulary>. バイク normally means a motorbike; 自転車 is the unambiguous everyday word for a bicycle.

contextSentences.ja: 兄はバイクで会社に通っている。
contextSentences.en: My older brother commutes to work by motorcycle.

contextSentences.ja: 雨の日は危ないので、バイクには乗らない。
contextSentences.en: I don't ride my motorcycle on rainy days because it's dangerous.

packs.title: People on Screen & Stage
packs.description: Common social and entertainment words for couples, fans, members, leaders, guests, performers, characters, heroes, and events.

words.meaningMnemonic: Two cups click handles and refuse to be separated while a sign flashes <reading>COUPLE</reading>. The paired cups have become a romantic <vocabulary>couple</vocabulary>. カップル usually refers to two people in a romantic relationship, not merely any pair of objects.

contextSentences.ja: 公園で若いカップルが写真を撮っていた。
contextSentences.en: A young couple was taking photos in the park.

contextSentences.ja: 二人は大学時代から付き合っているカップルです。
contextSentences.en: They have been a couple since their university days.

words.meaningMnemonic: A paper <reading>FAN</reading> buys a concert ticket and waves itself wildly from the front row. It is not cooling anyone today; it is a devoted <vocabulary>fan</vocabulary> of the singer. ファン commonly means an admirer, though the same spelling can mean an electric fan when context points to the appliance.

contextSentences.ja: 彼女はそのバンドの長年のファンです。
contextSentences.en: She has been a fan of that band for many years.

contextSentences.ja: 試合のあと、選手たちはファンに手を振った。
contextSentences.en: After the game, the players waved to their fans.

words.meaningMnemonic: Each <reading>MEMBER</reading> holds one piece of a broken stage; only when everyone joins can the show continue. Every participant is a <vocabulary>member</vocabulary> of the group. メンバー is common for teams, bands, clubs, projects, and event participants.

contextSentences.ja: 新しいメンバーをみんなに紹介します。
contextSentences.en: I'll introduce the new member to everyone.

contextSentences.ja: バンドのメンバー全員がステージに集まった。
contextSentences.en: All of the band members gathered on stage.

words.meaningMnemonic: A glowing arrow labeled <reading>LEADER</reading> walks at the front and pulls a lost team out of a maze. The person setting direction is the <vocabulary>leader</vocabulary>. リーダー is common for team or group leadership; 指導者 can sound more formal or institutional.

contextSentences.ja: 彼がこのプロジェクトのリーダーです。
contextSentences.en: He is the leader of this project.

contextSentences.ja: 登山では経験のある人をリーダーに選んだ。
contextSentences.en: An experienced person was chosen as the leader for the climb.

words.meaningMnemonic: A red carpet rolls itself toward the door and spells <reading>GUEST</reading> under one visitor's feet. The honored visitor is today's <vocabulary>guest</vocabulary>. ゲスト is especially common for invited performers, speakers, hotel users, and program guests.

contextSentences.ja: 今日の番組には特別なゲストが登場します。
contextSentences.en: A special guest will appear on today's program.

contextSentences.ja: ホテルのゲストは無料でプールを利用できる。
contextSentences.en: Hotel guests can use the pool for free.

words.meaningMnemonic: An <reading>IDOL</reading> statue jumps off its pedestal, grabs a microphone, and performs for a sea of coordinated glow sticks. This admired performer is a Japanese <vocabulary>pop idol</vocabulary>. アイドル usually means a carefully promoted young entertainer, not only an object of worship.

contextSentences.ja: 妹は人気アイドルの歌を毎日聞いている。
contextSentences.en: My younger sister listens to songs by a popular idol every day.

contextSentences.ja: アイドルのコンサート会場で限定グッズを買った。
contextSentences.en: I bought limited-edition merchandise at the idol's concert venue.

words.meaningMnemonic: A suitcase marked <reading>TALENT</reading> opens on television, and a comedian, host, and singer all spring out. In Japanese media, each visible entertainer can be a <vocabulary>TV personality</vocabulary>. タレント usually labels a media performer rather than the abstract ability called “talent.”

contextSentences.ja: そのタレントは料理番組にもよく出演している。
contextSentences.en: That TV personality also appears frequently on cooking shows.

contextSentences.ja: 人気タレントが新しい商品の広告に出演した。
contextSentences.en: A popular celebrity appeared in an advertisement for the new product.

words.meaningMnemonic: A storybook shouts <reading>CHARACTER</reading>, and its hero climbs off the page to rearrange the plot. The living drawing is a fictional <vocabulary>character</vocabulary>. キャラクター can also mean a person's distinctive personality or a designed mascot.

contextSentences.ja: このアニメで一番好きなキャラクターは誰ですか。
contextSentences.en: Who is your favorite character in this anime?

contextSentences.ja: 主人公のキャラクターが原作とは少し違う。
contextSentences.en: The protagonist's personality is slightly different from the original work.

contextSentences.ja: 町のキャラクターが祭りに登場した。
contextSentences.en: The town mascot appeared at the festival.

words.readingMap: キャ・ラ・ク・タ・ー

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>HERO</reading> tears open a cape, catches a falling train, and sets it gently back on the rails. The rescuer becomes everyone's <vocabulary>hero</vocabulary>. ヒーロー is common for fictional heroes and admired real people; 英雄 often has a more historical or grand tone.

contextSentences.ja: 子どもの頃、このヒーローに憧れていた。
contextSentences.en: I admired this hero when I was a child.

contextSentences.ja: 勇気を出して助けた消防士は、町のヒーローになった。
contextSentences.en: The firefighter who bravely came to the rescue became the town's hero.

words.meaningMnemonic: An <reading>EVENT</reading> calendar bursts open and releases a stage, food stalls, and a cheering crowd into the square. The organized occasion is a public <vocabulary>event</vocabulary>. イベント usually suggests a planned activity, promotion, festival, or in-game occurrence rather than any incident whatsoever.

contextSentences.ja: 週末に駅前で音楽イベントが開かれる。
contextSentences.en: A music event will be held near the station this weekend.

contextSentences.ja: 店の開店記念イベントに多くの客が集まった。
contextSentences.en: Many customers gathered for the store's grand-opening event.

packs.title: Fitness & Everyday Wellness
packs.description: Practical words for masks, contact lenses, glasses, jogging, hiking, yoga, gyms, pools, stretching, and training.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>MASK</reading> stretches across an entire train carriage and covers every nose at once. The protective covering is a <vocabulary>face mask</vocabulary>. In ordinary health contexts, マスク means a mask worn over the nose and mouth.

contextSentences.ja: 花粉が多い日はマスクをつけます。
contextSentences.en: I wear a face mask on days with a lot of pollen.

contextSentences.ja: 病院に入る前に、新しいマスクに替えた。
contextSentences.en: Before entering the hospital, I changed into a fresh mask.

words.meaningMnemonic: A tiny <reading>CONTACT</reading> lens makes contact with a giant eye, then snaps into place like a shield. The clear disc is a <vocabulary>contact lens</vocabulary>. In eye-care conversation, コンタクト is the ordinary abbreviation of コンタクトレンズ.

contextSentences.ja: 今日はコンタクトではなくメガネをかけています。
contextSentences.en: Today I'm wearing glasses instead of contact lenses.

contextSentences.ja: 目が乾いたので、コンタクトを外した。
contextSentences.en: My eyes felt dry, so I took out my contact lenses.

words.meaningMnemonic: A giant <reading>VITAMIN</reading> capsule cracks open and fills the kitchen with glowing fruit and vegetables. Every color carries a different <vocabulary>vitamin</vocabulary>. ビタミン appears in names such as ビタミンC and in compounds such as ビタミン不足, vitamin deficiency.

contextSentences.ja: 野菜からビタミンを摂るようにしています。
contextSentences.en: I try to get vitamins from vegetables.

contextSentences.ja: この果物にはビタミンCが多く含まれている。
contextSentences.en: This fruit contains a lot of vitamin C.

words.meaningMnemonic: A pair of shoes begins <reading>JOGGING</reading> around the park before its owner wakes up. Their steady easy run is <vocabulary>jogging</vocabulary>, not an all-out sprint. ジョギングする is the common verb phrase for going jogging.

contextSentences.ja: 健康のために毎朝ジョギングしています。
contextSentences.en: I go jogging every morning for my health.

contextSentences.ja: 雨の日はジョギングを休んで、家で運動する。
contextSentences.en: On rainy days, I skip jogging and exercise at home.

words.meaningMnemonic: A trail sign marked <reading>HIKING</reading> grows legs and leads a line of backpacks up the mountain. The whole cheerful procession is <vocabulary>hiking</vocabulary>. ハイキング usually suggests a day walk for pleasure; more serious mountain climbing is 登山.

contextSentences.ja: 秋に家族と山へハイキングに行った。
contextSentences.en: I went hiking in the mountains with my family in autumn.

contextSentences.ja: 初心者向けのハイキングコースを選んだ。
contextSentences.en: We chose a hiking trail suitable for beginners.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>YOGA</reading> mat twists itself into a perfect tree pose and calmly waits for you to copy it. The balancing practice is <vocabulary>yoga</vocabulary>. ヨガをする is the everyday way to say that you do or practice yoga.

contextSentences.ja: 寝る前に二十分ヨガをしています。
contextSentences.en: I do twenty minutes of yoga before bed.

contextSentences.ja: 週末のヨガ教室で呼吸の仕方を習った。
contextSentences.en: I learned breathing techniques in a weekend yoga class.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>GYM</reading> folds its treadmills and weights into a vending machine, then unfolds when a member scans a card. The workout facility is a <vocabulary>gym</vocabulary>. ジム commonly means a fitness gym; 体育館 is a school-style gymnasium or sports hall.

contextSentences.ja: 仕事の後でジムに通っています。
contextSentences.en: I go to the gym after work.

contextSentences.ja: このジムには初心者向けの器具もそろっている。
contextSentences.en: This gym also has equipment for beginners.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>POOL</reading> rises from the ground and chases overheated swimmers until they jump in. The moving rectangle of water is a <vocabulary>swimming pool</vocabulary>. Without another cue, プール most often means a swimming pool.

contextSentences.ja: 夏は市民プールで泳ぎます。
contextSentences.en: I swim at the public pool in summer.

contextSentences.ja: 大会のため、今日はプールが貸し切りです。
contextSentences.en: The pool is reserved today for a competition.

words.meaningMnemonic: A rubber band shouts <reading>STRETCH!</reading> and pulls every stiff arm and leg gently toward the ceiling. The warm-up movement is <vocabulary>stretching</vocabulary>. ストレッチする usually means to do flexibility exercises, especially before or after activity.

contextSentences.ja: 走る前に足をストレッチした。
contextSentences.en: I stretched my legs before running.

contextSentences.ja: 毎朝の軽いストレッチで体が動かしやすくなった。
contextSentences.en: A little stretching every morning has made it easier for me to move.

words.meaningMnemonic: A tiny <reading>TRAINING</reading> train circles a gym, adding one weight to every carriage on each lap. The repeated practice becomes a serious <vocabulary>workout</vocabulary>. トレーニング can mean physical exercise or structured practice for a skill.

contextSentences.ja: 週に三回、筋力トレーニングをしている。
contextSentences.en: I do strength training three times a week.

contextSentences.ja: 新人は接客のトレーニングを受けた。
contextSentences.en: The new employee received customer-service training.

words.readingMap: ト・レ・ー・ニ・ン・グ

packs.title: Kitchen Tools & Flavors
packs.description: Everyday kitchen words for sauces, spices, recipes, pans, ovens, microwaves, grills, blenders, wine, and timers.

words.meaningMnemonic: A bottle of <reading>SAUCE</reading> paints a brown river across a plate and floats the fried food away. The river is unmistakably <vocabulary>sauce</vocabulary>. ソース can be sauce generally, but on a Japanese table it often points to thick Worcestershire-style sauce.

contextSentences.ja: とんかつにソースをかけて食べた。
contextSentences.en: I poured sauce over the pork cutlet before eating it.

contextSentences.ja: パスタのソースを弱火で温めた。
contextSentences.en: I warmed the pasta sauce over low heat.

words.meaningMnemonic: A jar labeled <reading>SPICE</reading> sneezes a red cloud into the stew and wakes every flavor at once. One pinch of the <vocabulary>spice</vocabulary> changes the whole pot. スパイス can be a culinary spice or, figuratively, an exciting extra element.

contextSentences.ja: このカレーにはいろいろなスパイスが入っている。
contextSentences.en: This curry contains many different spices.

contextSentences.ja: 肉にスパイスを振ってから焼いた。
contextSentences.en: I sprinkled spices on the meat before grilling it.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>RECIPE</reading> card sprouts hands and measures every ingredient before the cook can make a mistake. Its ordered instructions form the <vocabulary>recipe</vocabulary>. レシピ is used for cooking instructions and can extend to a figurative formula or how-to guide.

contextSentences.ja: ネットで簡単なパスタのレシピを探した。
contextSentences.en: I looked online for an easy pasta recipe.

contextSentences.ja: 初めて作る料理なので、レシピどおりに作った。
contextSentences.en: Since it was my first time making the dish, I followed the recipe exactly.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>FRY PAN</reading> flaps its handle like a wing and flies breakfast from the stove to the table. The airborne cookware is a <vocabulary>frying pan</vocabulary>. フライパン is the ordinary shallow pan for frying or sautéing.

contextSentences.ja: フライパンで野菜を炒めます。
contextSentences.en: I stir-fry vegetables in a frying pan.

contextSentences.ja: 熱したフライパンに卵を割り入れた。
contextSentences.en: I cracked an egg into the heated frying pan.

words.meaningMnemonic: An <reading>OVEN</reading> opens its door and launches a perfectly baked loaf like a warm rocket. The enclosed baking appliance is an <vocabulary>oven</vocabulary>. オーブン usually means a baking or roasting oven, distinct from a microwave-only 電子レンジ.

contextSentences.ja: オーブンを百八十度に温めてください。
contextSentences.en: Please preheat the oven to 180 degrees.

contextSentences.ja: クッキーをオーブンで十五分焼いた。
contextSentences.en: I baked the cookies in the oven for fifteen minutes.

contextSentences.ja: この容器はオーブンでは使えません。
contextSentences.en: This container cannot be used in the oven.

words.meaningMnemonic: A cooking <reading>RANGE</reading> shrinks into a microwave and heats dinner in thirty seconds. In the kitchen, the compact appliance is often a <vocabulary>microwave oven</vocabulary>. 電子レンジ is fully explicit, while レンジ alone may also mean a stove or range.

contextSentences.ja: 冷めたスープをレンジで温めた。
contextSentences.en: I warmed the cold soup in the microwave.

contextSentences.ja: 新しい台所には三口のガスレンジがある。
contextSentences.en: The new kitchen has a three-burner gas range.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>GRILL</reading> snaps shut like a metal jaw and returns a fish with perfect char marks. The hot rack is a <vocabulary>grill</vocabulary>. In Japanese kitchens, グリル often means the small built-in fish grill beneath the stovetop.

contextSentences.ja: 魚をグリルで十分ほど焼いた。
contextSentences.en: I grilled the fish for about ten minutes.

contextSentences.ja: 肉をグリルで焼いて、表面に焼き色をつけた。
contextSentences.en: I cooked the meat on the grill and browned the surface.

words.meaningMnemonic: A <reading>MIXER</reading> whirls fruit, ice, and the recipe card into one bright smoothie. The countertop machine is a <vocabulary>blender</vocabulary>. In everyday Japanese kitchens, ミキサー often means a jug blender rather than only an English-style stand or hand mixer.

contextSentences.ja: ミキサーでバナナジュースを作った。
contextSentences.en: I made a banana smoothie in the blender.

contextSentences.ja: 柔らかく煮た野菜をミキサーにかけてスープにした。
contextSentences.en: I blended the softened vegetables into soup.

words.meaningMnemonic: A bottle of <reading>WINE</reading> grows grapevine arms and pours itself carefully into every glass. The fermented grape drink is <vocabulary>wine</vocabulary>. 赤ワイン and 白ワイン distinguish red and white wine.

contextSentences.ja: 夕食に赤ワインを一杯飲みました。
contextSentences.en: I drank a glass of red wine with dinner.

contextSentences.ja: このソースには料理用のワインを少し加える。
contextSentences.en: Add a little cooking wine to this sauce.

words.meaningMnemonic: A kitchen <reading>TIMER</reading> sprouts legs, chases the cook, and rings until the cake leaves the oven. The noisy countdown device is a <vocabulary>timer</vocabulary>. タイマーをセットする means to set a timer.

contextSentences.ja: タイマーを五分にセットしてください。
contextSentences.en: Please set the timer for five minutes.

contextSentences.ja: タイマーが鳴ったら、オーブンからパンを出して。
contextSentences.en: When the timer goes off, take the bread out of the oven.
